Research presents conflicting findings on whether children learn language skills from television. [d1] Some studies suggest that educational programs, especially when co-viewed with an adult, can improve vocabulary, comprehension, and cognitive outcomes — with a large-scale meta-analysis noting that educational programming may be beneficial for child language, though caution is warranted as program quality varies [d1][d2][d7]. Overall, the evidence suggests that any language benefit from television is highly conditional — depending on the quality of the program, whether an adult co-watches, and the child's age — and is almost universally overshadowed by the value of direct, in-person social interaction [d1][d2][d10].
